method: Read-only. Files read in full or in cited ranges; targeted grep; node -e for digest experiments and kernel import; bash certification/verify-freeze.sh (read-only) and certification/verify-freeze.test.sh with TMPDIR confined to the scratchpad. No builds, no full suites, no network, no secrets read. Local userData evidence files were probed for existence/row counts only (none exist).
architecture_invariant_under_audit: HUMAN -> CONTROL -> COMPUTE -> EVIDENCE -> VERIFICATION -> HUMAN DECISION. AI proposes; policy/authority governs; Computer-B executes; Computer-A verifies; Human decides. AI never authorizes; client never final authority; network != authorization; stale authorization rejected.

chain_representability.question: Is INTENT->AUTHORITY->POLICY->ACTION->EXECUTION->RESULT->EVIDENCE->VERIFICATION representable end-to-end today?
chain_representability.answer: PARTIALLY, as a single-row projection with declared gaps. The kernel models every stage in memory; the persisted ActionRecord keeps ACTION, EXECUTION, RESULT, EVIDENCE (record_time) and VERIFICATION, but INTENT is a constant string that is not persisted, AUTHORITY is reduced to a verdict string + actor (the Approval object, approver, expiry, fencing token are discarded), and POLICY has no version anywhere in the product. There is no HUMAN DECISION stage after VERIFICATION in the desktop evidence model, and the backend HumanDecision path is unreachable in production.

INTENT.kernel: TransitionRequest.intent + purpose (types.d.ts:122-123); adapters pass fixed literals, e.g. 'send a single reviewer-confirmed message via the connector' (sendTransition.ts:218)
INTENT.persisted: NO (readBack.ts:125 'purpose' in NOT_PERSISTED). correlationId (asst_<uuid>) persisted optionally as causal-episode identity (actionRecord.ts:118-134); confirmedAt persisted optionally as the human confirm instant (actionRecord.ts:160-169)

AUTHORITY.kernel: Approval{approvalId,transitionId,approver,action,scope,resourceVersion,purpose,policyVersion,issuedAt,expiresAt,consumed} minted by the adapter from `confirmed:boolean` with approver = the requesting actor (sendTransition.ts:195-209; governedAction.ts:283-297); kernel checks approver.type!=='AI', SoD (only when declared), binding, scope, expiry (kernel.js:122-173)
AUTHORITY.persisted: Only `verdict` (string) and `actor` (verbatim). The approval object, approvalId, expiry and fencing token are NOT persisted (readBack.ts:127-128). BoundDecisionClaim path persists decisionId+bindingDigest+claimNonce into ExecutionSession (executeEngine.ts:155-157).
AUTHORITY.note: AI cannot self-authorize in the kernel (MODEL_SELF_AUTHORIZATION, kernel.js:111-130) — MEASURED. Human self-approval (requester == approver, type HUMAN) is accepted because no sodActions are declared for send/action/import policies (sendTransition.ts:231-234; governedAction.ts:318-321; importTransition.ts:217-222) — DERIVED.

POLICY.kernel: PolicyStore(grants, version) evaluate(actor, action, consequence); policyVersion literal 'm365-send-policy-1' / 'm365-action-policy-1' (connectors/index.ts:628; governedAction.ts:68)
POLICY.persisted: NO (readBack.ts:126). certification/baseline.json:15-16 records policy_version as ABSENT product-wide; boundDecisionClaim.ts:24-29 excludes policyVersion deliberately.

ACTION.persisted: connectorId, accountId, actionId, recipients, subject/body fingerprints, transitionId (content-addressed idempotency identity), admissionRef (actionRecord.ts:504-520)

RESULT.persisted: outcome = semanticOutcome (ACKNOWLEDGED is a transport ack, never verified: sendTransition.ts:66-74,274-276)

VERIFICATION.producers: readBackReconciler (production BackgroundService, 60 s tick, mail.send only, M365 Graph Sent Items/Inbox read-back, width bound 120 s), journalPostEvidence (in-kernel post-state re-read), s16VerifyRun (compile-gated, not production)

Backend HumanDecision exists in schema but is withheld (403) in production.

what_verification_means_in_code.kernel_verification: Structural equality JSON.stringify(observedPostState) === JSON.stringify(expectedPostState) over the injected ResourceStore, subject-bound (NPL-23), UNKNOWN when UNOBSERVABLE (kernel.js:326-352). The 'authoritative source' is `resource-store:authoritative` — in every desktop adapter this is an in-memory ResourceStore the adapter itself writes via resources.put(...) inside the effect (sendTransition.ts:237,264,287; governedAction.ts:324,343,363; importTransition.ts:232,248). For Profile A (send, governedAction) post-state is set UNOBSERVABLE so VERIFIED is structurally unreachable; for import the post-state is read back from the destination so VERIFIED is reachable.
what_verification_means_in_code.independent_read_back_seam22: reconciliation/readBack.ts reconstructs request -> verdict -> execution -> observation -> verification from PERSISTED ActionRecord rows only, never from an execute() return value; readBackFromDisk(dir, scopeTenantId, ref) uses createActionRecordReader(dir) — a fresh ActionRecordStore over the persisted file with a query-only surface — so it can catch divergence between process memory and durable evidence (readBack.ts:1-35,237-255; actionRecord.ts:616-630). Requires at least one ref (requestId|transitionId|correlationId); listing is refused. Pinned by reconciliation/readBack.test.ts, fp39Closure.test.ts, compositionRoot.test.ts, fanOutIdentity.test.ts.
what_verification_means_in_code.reconciler: readBackReconciler.ts: READ store -> CLASSIFY -> RECORD terminal -> STOP; HOLD is terminal; never executes; never promotes UNKNOWN; provenance {source:'readBackReconciler', method, oracle:'m365ReadBack:sentItems+inbox'}; subject limb compared by hashing the observed subject with recordFingerprint (D2); interval requestTime<=effect<=at bounded to 120 s (D1). Wired as a BackgroundService in serviceManager.ts:146, started by runtimeCore.ts:4130; fan-out perWorkspace:true to compensate F-P45.
what_verification_means_in_code.vocabulary_authority: verificationTerminals.ts: SUCCESS={VERIFIED_SUCCESS}; FAILURE={VERIFY_FAILED, VERIFIED_FAILURE}; everything else (HOLD, UNKNOWN, VERIFY_PENDING, EXECUTED_ACK, VERIFIED_NOOP, unrecognised) is unresolved. Deny-by-default.
what_verification_means_in_code.what_verification_is_NOT: No verifier outside the executing process/custody exists in code. No signature, counter-signature, or attestation is produced over any ActionRecord. 'Computer-A' does not appear anywhere in the repo (grep docs/ certification/: 0 hits); it exists only in the Downloads evidence corpus. VERIFIER_IDENTITY = NOT_DESIGNATED (REVIEWER-BRIEFING-PACK.md:132; GATE-STATUS-BOARD.md:37).
what_verification_means_in_code.classification: MEASURED except the Computer-A statement which is ABSENT-in-repo

tamper_evidence_assessment.action_records: NOT tamper-evident. Append-only is a property of the writer code, not of the file: the persisted JSON array carries no per-row digest, no previous-hash, no signature, no monotonic counter. recordFingerprint.ts:10 claims 'TAMPER-EVIDENCE' but the function only proves that a subject/body matches a hash; a row's other fields (verdict, executed, outcome, verification) can be edited on disk without detection. Envelope quarantine (storeEnvelope.ts) detects CORRUPTION, not tampering. (MEASURED + DERIVED)

digest_vs_receipt_vs_transport_vs_custod.digest_equality: Proves two byte sequences are identical. Present as: artifactSha256 + .sha256 sidecar (make-release-manifest.cjs:103,164, Windows only); feed sha512 vs file (verify-release-artifacts.cjs:112-172); SOURCE_DIGEST/TREE/HEAD (TR-GPR-01/03); bindingDigest (boundDecisionClaim.ts:74-76); STDOUT_STDERR_SHA256 (TR-GPR-03:20); recordFingerprint sha256-16 (64-bit truncation — adequate for privacy/comparison, not a collision-resistant integrity digest). Digest equality says NOTHING about who produced the bytes, when, or whether they were delivered.
digest_vs_receipt_vs_transport_vs_custod.receipt: An assertion by a counterparty that it accepted an object. Present only as: Graph HTTP 202 -> 'ACKNOWLEDGED' (explicitly 'accepted for delivery, NOT verified', sendTransition.ts:69), and PauseCloud StorageReceipt (design-only, not implemented). TR-GPR-03 execution records and the ActionRecord row are SELF-issued observer records, not counterparty receipts. No counter-signed receipt exists anywhere.
digest_vs_receipt_vs_transport_vs_custod.transport: Movement of an object between custodies with an identity-preserving record. In code: NONE for evidence. Update feed + sha512 is transport integrity for BINARIES to end users, not evidence to Computer-A. A/B transport is manual and, per the evidence corpus, basename-keyed and overwrite-prone.
digest_vs_receipt_vs_transport_vs_custod.custody: Who holds the object and under what control. Expressed only as self-declared JSON fields (CUSTODY: COMPUTER_B) and git author strings of a machine identity ('NeuroPause Gate Closure <noreply@anthropic.com>'). No signature/attestation binds custody; verify-freeze.sh prints that the repo cannot attribute a change to a human. Custody transitions are unrecorded by any instrument in the repo.
digest_vs_receipt_vs_transport_vs_custod.classification: MEASURED for repo facts; DECLARED for corpus facts; DERIVED for the distinctions

ActionRecord row schema: id act_<uuid>, correlationId?, at, requestId, transitionId, requestTime?, eventTime?, confirmedAt?, actor, tenantId, connectorId, accountId, actionId, recipients{to,cc,bcc}, subjectFingerprint, bodyFingerprint, verdict, executed, outcome, admissionRef, verification|null; verification = {terminal, internetMessageId, at, provenance?{source,method,oracle}, effectTime?}.
ActionRecord rows have no per-row digest, no previous-hash, no signature; the file is {schemaVersion:1, records:[…]} written via unique tmp + rename with Windows rename retry.

ActionRecordStore declares append-only retention (no cap, TTL, eviction or delete path); observe/observeGovernance only push; recordVerification mutates verification in place with monotonicity (settled terminals never replaced; refusal logged).
ActionRecordStore.flush() (S162) awaits every tracked in-flight persist including fire-and-forget governance emits; registered on the shutdown barrier as 'action-records'.

Three production producers of ActionRecord rows: execution-class observe after governedSend (fire-and-forget), governance-class observeGovernance for DENY/NOT_EVALUATED at the live-brain gate, and journal.post evidence in finance.
ActionRecord.tenantId holds a WORKSPACE id (F-P45): the send observer passes tenantId: deps.workspaceId(); the reconciler compensates with perWorkspace:true and documents a migration owed.

transitionId is content-addressed: m365-send:<sha256(tenant|connector|account|action|JSON.stringify(params))>; two runs with identical params share transitionId/idem by design; correlationId (asst_<uuid>) is the only causal separator and is optional.
The kernel EvidenceStore is an in-memory array of frozen {transitionId, stage, at, detail}; append-only class; no digest; no persistence.
Every desktop adapter constructs a fresh EvidenceStore per call and no non-test code reads it (.forTransition( has 0 non-test callers); the kernel's per-stage evidence ledger is discarded.

Kernel stage log vocabulary: REQUESTED, RECOVERY_BYPASS, DENIED, RELATIONSHIP_ASSESSMENT, HOLD, BLOCKED, CLAIM_LOST, CLAIMED, IDEMPOTENT_REPLAY, REPLAY_UNRESOLVED, RECONCILED, PREFLIGHT_PRIOR_ATTEMPT, EXECUTION_ERROR, EXECUTED, VERIFICATION.

facts.fact: Kernel forbids AI self-authorization: an AI actor needs an approval and an AI approver is BLOCKED (MODEL_SELF_AUTHORIZATION); approval binding/scope/expiry/constraints enforced.

In all three desktop adapters the approval is minted from confirmed:boolean with approver = the requesting actor (type HUMAN), and no separation-of-duties action is declared, so requester == approver is accepted by the kernel.
All three adapters pass evidence: [] to the kernel, so the evidenceFreshness guard (NP-NC-06) has nothing to evaluate.

Kernel verification is STRUCTURAL_EQUALITY of JSON.stringify(observed) vs expected over the injected ResourceStore; UNKNOWN when UNOBSERVABLE or subject-mismatch; the proposition source is 'resource-store:authoritative'.

For send and governedAction (Profile A) the adapter writes UNOBSERVABLE into the ResourceStore after the effect, so kernel verification is always UNKNOWN and VERIFIED_SUCCESS is structurally unreachable; ACKNOWLEDGED is a transport ack only.

The kernel's 'authoritative' ResourceStore in every desktop adapter is an in-memory store written by the adapter itself inside the effect; kernel verification is therefore not independent of the executing process.

importTransition reads the post-state back from the destination, so the kernel can reach VERIFIED; classifyImport splits VERIFIED_SUCCESS into VERIFIED_SUCCESS / VERIFIED_NOOP and passes VERIFIED_FAILURE, DEVIATION, UNKNOWN verbatim.
